candidates.original_title: Warm thoughts: Attachment anxiety and sensitivity to temperature cues
candidates.description: Individuals with high anxious attachment report heightened preferences for warm foods when attachment concerns are activated by reflecting on a romantic breakup
candidates.citation_sentence: In his recent article, Vess (2012) was the first to integrate research on attachment anxiety with research linking physical temperature to perceptions of intimacy (i.e., intimacy is associated with physical warmth, whereas social isolation is associated with coldness; IJzerman & Semin, 2009; Zhong & Leonardelli, 2008).
candidates.notes: Sample 1 (N=219) of LeBel & Campbell (2013); direct replication of Vess (2012) Study 1; authors explicitly state they did not replicate the finding. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
